A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glass-forming tendency of Zr-based alloys is governed by the melt viscosity and the atomic mobility of the undercooleld liquid.

the glass forming ability of a metallic liquid is not only determined by thermodynamic factors but also strongly influenced by kinetic factors, which are related to the atomic structure and dynamics of the melt.
a high glass-forming ability is not a direct consequence of a low crystal-melt inter-facial tension, but is rather a result of a high viscosity of the undercooded liquid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glass-forming capability of Zr-based bulk metallic glasses can be improved by lowering their melting temperature and/or increasing the liquidus undercooling.
the glass-forming abilities of bulk amorphous alloy systems can be enhanced by reducing the melt viscosity and/or by increasing the crystal-melt interdiffusion rate.
